<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/generate_reference.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Guardrails wrap the target in classifier models, so you can measure an attack against a *defended* system rather than a bare model. They are off unless you ask for them.

## `guardrails` {#guardrailsspec}

Classifier models that defend the target.

`before` checks each prompt and blocks an unsafe one before it reaches the
target; `after` checks the reply and withholds an unsafe one. Both fail open:
an unavailable or unparseable classifier lets the text through, so a
misconfigured guardrail never blocks the whole run. Use this to measure an
attack against a *defended* target.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `before` | [GuardrailModelConfig](#guardrailmodelconfig) | unset | Classifier that checks each prompt before it reaches the target. |
| `after` | [GuardrailModelConfig](#guardrailmodelconfig) | unset | Classifier that checks each reply before it is returned. |

## `guardrails.before and guardrails.after` {#guardrailmodelconfig}

A guardrail: a classifier model that decides whether a text is safe.

Takes every field of [ModelConfig](target.md#modelconfig) (`name`, `connection`, `generation`, `options`), and also:

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_prompt` | string | unset | Replace the classifier's built-in instruction with your own. |

## Examples

**A safety classifier on both sides of the target**

```yaml
guardrails:
  before:
    name: llama-guard3:8b
    connection:
      provider: ollama
      type: OLLAMA
  after:
    name: llama-guard3:8b
    connection:
      provider: ollama
      type: OLLAMA
```
